layers.title: Climate normals at region points (NASA POWER)

source.name: NASA POWER Climatology API (MERRA-2)
source.licence: NASA open data; acknowledge NASA POWER
source.attribution: Data from the NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project funded through the NASA Earth Science Directorate Applied Science Program

layers.notes: Monthly means at about 0.5 degree resolution; they understate the extreme (99th percentile) design conditions used for cooling design. Not ASHRAE design data.

layers.title: US climate normals 1991-2020 (NOAA)

source.name: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991-2020
source.attribution: Source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information

layers.notes: Station may be up to 80 km from the market centroid. Normals are decadal; refresh interval is long.

layers.title: Interconnection facilities with 20+ networks (global)

source.name: PeeringDB (facilities, internet exchanges)
source.licence: PeeringDB Acceptable Use Policy (public data, attribution); only derived counts and unnamed points republished
source.attribution: Data from PeeringDB (peeringdb.com), used per its Acceptable Use Policy

layers.notes: Unnamed points; network counts self-reported by operators.

layers.title: Network facilities and exchanges near each market

source.name: PeeringDB (facilities, internet exchanges)
source.licence: PeeringDB Acceptable Use Policy (public data, attribution); only derived counts and unnamed points republished
source.attribution: Data from PeeringDB (peeringdb.com), used per its Acceptable Use Policy

layers.notes: Self-reported, user-maintained registry; undercounts private facilities and some regions. Counts are a connectivity proxy, not route diversity.

layers.title: Live indicator scores derived from fetched layers

source.name: Derived by Rackmere from the layers listed in each region's 'from' map
source.licence: Derived data; each input layer keeps its own licence and attribution
source.attribution: Computed from the cited source layers

layers.notes: Recomputed on every refresh. Educational proxies, not site data.

layers.title: US grid carbon intensity (eGRID subregion)

source.name: U.S. EPA eGRID2023 (subregion output emission rates)

layers.notes: Annual-average location-based rate; hourly and market-based values differ. Subregion found by point-in-polygon on EPA's service.

layers.title: National grid carbon intensity and clean share (Ember)
layers.notes: National averages applied to each market; the market-level grid can differ. Includes US regions' national value for context.

layers.title: FEMA National Risk Index (county)

source.name: FEMA National Risk Index
source.licence: US Government work (FEMA); data open, cite FEMA

layers.notes: County values, not site values. Scores are relative national percentiles of expected annual loss x social vulnerability / resilience, not probabilities.

layers.title: US seismic design ground motion (USGS)

source.name: USGS Seismic Design Web Services (ASCE 7-22, 2020 NEHRP-based hazard)

layers.notes: Design-code ground motion at the market centroid; site-specific hazard studies are needed for real sites.

layers.title: Governance indicators (World Bank WGI)

source.name: World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators
source.attribution: World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators (Kaufmann and Kraay), CC BY 4.0

layers.notes: Country-level perception indicators; not a prediction of project outcomes; says nothing about a city or state.

layers.title: US industrial electricity price by state

source.name: U.S. EIA, Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A (Form EIA-861M)
source.licence: US Government work, public domain (EIA asks for citation)

layers.notes: State-average industrial price for the latest month (preliminary). Not a utility tariff; excludes demand-charge detail.

layers.title: EU industrial electricity price (Eurostat)

source.name: Eurostat nrg_pc_205 (electricity prices for non-household consumers)

layers.notes: National half-yearly averages for a mid-size industrial band; large data centres often pay differently (own contracts). Bi-annual release.
layers.coverage: EU/EEA countries in the region set

layers.title: Grid proximity (substations and lines near each US market)

source.name: HIFLD Electric Substations and Transmission Lines
source.licence: Public domain (US Government HIFLD open data release)
source.attribution: Source: DHS/CISA HIFLD (mirror hosted on ArcGIS Online)

layers.notes: Proximity of high-voltage facilities is not capacity or headroom. Data vintage is that of the HIFLD release, which can be years old.

layers.title: Transmission lines at 345 kV and above (US, simplified)

source.name: HIFLD Electric Power Transmission Lines (public-domain US infrastructure data)
source.licence: Public domain (US Government HIFLD open data release); source field cites OpenStreetMap contributors for some segments
source.attribution: Source: DHS/CISA HIFLD Electric Power Transmission Lines (mirror hosted on ArcGIS Online); some geometry derived from OpenStreetMap contributors

layers.notes: Simplified to about 1 km; coarse visual overlay, not engineering data.

layers.title: Substations at 345 kV and above (US)

source.name: HIFLD Electric Substations (public-domain US infrastructure data)
source.licence: Public domain (US Government HIFLD open data release)
source.attribution: Source: DHS/CISA HIFLD Electric Substations (mirror hosted on ArcGIS Online)

layers.notes: Positions rounded to 0.01 degree (about 1 km). Voltage as recorded; may be outdated. No headroom/capacity information is public.

layers.title: Water stress (WRI Aqueduct 4.0)

source.name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 Water Risk Atlas (baseline annual)
source.attribution: World Resources Institute, Aqueduct 4.0 (Kuzma et al. 2023), CC BY 4.0

layers.notes: Admin-1 or country area-weighted mean, not the sub-basin at the site: a point-in-basin lookup needs GIS tooling. Local supply and water rights can differ strongly.
